text: Canberra is the capital city of Australia. It was selected as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne and became the seat of the federal government in 1927.
Pride and Prejudice is an 1813 novel by the English author Jane Austen. The story follows Elizabeth Bennet and her relationship with Mr Darcy.
Gold is a chemical element with the symbol Au, from the Latin word aurum. It has atomic number 79 and is a dense, soft metal.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System, with a mass more than twice that of all the other planets combined. It is a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium.
Albert Einstein published the theory of general relativity in 1915. The theory describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood through the circulatory system. It delivers oxygen and nutrients to tissues and removes carbon dioxide.
Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, is Earth's highest mountain above sea level at about 8,849 metres.
The Apollo 11 mission landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the lunar surface in July 1969, the first crewed Moon landing.
The yen is the official currency of Japan. It is one of the most traded currencies in the foreign exchange market.
The Amazon is the longest river in South America and carries more water than any other river on Earth.
The Mona Lisa is a portrait painted by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci in the early sixteenth century. It hangs in the Louvre in Paris.
Mitochondria generate most of the chemical energy needed by the cell in the form of ATP, which is why they are described as the powerhouse of the cell.
The cheetah is the fastest land animal, able to reach speeds of around 100 kilometres per hour in short bursts.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceans, covering about one third of the planet's surface.
The British computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.
Diamond is the hardest naturally occurring material, rating 10 on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness.
Ottawa, located in the province of Ontario, is the capital city of Canada and home to Parliament Hill.
Python is a high-level programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil, and use sunlight to produce glucose and release oxygen.
Mars is often called the Red Planet because iron oxide on its surface gives it a reddish appearance.
Charles Darwin proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection in his 1859 book On the Origin of Species.
Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan. It replaced Karachi as the capital in the 1960s and is located near Rawalpindi.
The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert in the world, covering around nine million square kilometres.
Hydrogen is the chemical element with atomic number 1. It is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe.
In its 2025 sustainability report, GreenLeaf Manufacturing disclosed Scope 1 emissions of 12,500 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, a 6 percent decrease from 2024.
GreenLeaf Manufacturing sourced 64% of its electricity from renewable energy in 2025, mainly through rooftop solar and a wind power purchase agreement.
GreenLeaf Manufacturing has committed to reaching net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across its operations by 2040.
Australia's largest city by population is Sydney, which is famous for its harbour and opera house.
Charlotte Bronte was an English novelist best known for Jane Eyre, published in 1847.
Silver has the chemical symbol Ag and is prized for its high electrical conductivity.
Saturn is the second-largest planet in the Solar System and is known for its prominent ring system.
Isaac Newton formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation in the seventeenth century.
The liver filters blood, produces bile, and plays a central role in metabolism.
K2 is the second-highest mountain on Earth and lies on the China-Pakistan border.
Toronto is the most populous city in Canada and the capital of the province of Ontario.
Java is a class-based, object-oriented programming language released by Sun Microsystems in 1995.
Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan and its main seaport and financial centre.
GreenLeaf Manufacturing reported that its employee training hours increased by 18 percent in 2025.
The Gobi Desert is a large, cold desert spanning parts of northern China and southern Mongolia.
Gregor Mendel is known as the father of modern genetics for his experiments on pea plants.
Helium is a noble gas with atomic number 2 and is used to fill balloons and cool superconducting magnets.
